la:adj:compos.gloss: having mastery, control, or power over something (coupled with genitive)
senses: having mastery, control, or power over something (coupled with genitive)
sharing (especially in the guilt of something)
la:adj:compos.html:
com-pŏs (conp-), pŏtis, adj.
potis
,
having the mastery, control, or power over a thing, master of, partaking of, possessing, participating or sharing in, guilty of, etc. (very freq. and class.); constr. usu. with gen., more rarely with abl., or absol.
With gen.: animi, of a sane mind, * : mentis,; ; ; ; ; : territum et vix mentis suae compotem opprimere,: nec satis compotem mentis... deferunt,: sui,; ; : rationis et consilii,; cf. : libertatis,: patriae,; : ejus doni,: hujus urbis,: bellicae laudis,: spei,; : voti, having obtained or gratified one's wish, ; ; ; ; ; ; ; cf. votorum,.—
With abl.: qui essent animo et scientiā compotes,: corpore atque animo,: mente,: praedā ingenti,.—
Absol.: vix compos (sc. mentis) Imilce,.—
Referring to misfortune or guilt, sharing in, participating in, confederate in, etc. (anteclass. and post-Aug.).
With gen.: miseriarum,: probri, Naev. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 6 Rib.): culpae,: sceleris,.—
With abl.: magnis et multis malis, Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 36 Rib.).—
Transf., of the thing: compote voto,.

la:noun:complexus.html:
complexus (con-), ūs, m.
complector
,
a surrounding, encompassing, encircling, embracing, embrace, etc. (class. in prose and poetry).
Lit.
Prop.
Of things (rare): aether Omnia avido complexu cetera saepsit,; so : qui (mundus) omnia complexu suo coërcet et continet,; : lapides alligati complexu silicis,by a binding,.—
Of persons: secutae conlocutiones cum Trebonio complexusque,: corporum,: e complexu parentum abreptos filios ad necem ducere,: ubi complexu coierunt membra tenaci,in a mutual close embrace,: complexu matris avellere natam,; cf. ; ; ; ; ; ; : Venerio,in copulation,.—In plur., * ; ; ; ; .—Rarely (like complector itself), of hostile embrace, close combat: in Martis complexu cadere,: armorum,; cf. of a serpent: longis amplexibus illos necat,: luctari complexu,.—
Transf., as a measure, the reach: (cedrus) crassitudinis ad trium hominum conplexum,.—
Trop.
A connection in discourse (very freq. in Quint.): vitium non est in sensu, sed in complexu,; cf. : brevis verborum,: sermonis,: in complexu loquendi serieque,: legum aliorumque scriptorum,: causarum,; : rerum, personarum, temporum, et saep.—
A friendly embracing, love, affectionate relation, etc.: venisti in sinum et complexum tuae mimulae,; cf.: res publica Pompeii filium suo sinu complexuque recipiet,; : totius gentis humanae,; : at tu easdem artes in complexu, oculis, auribus habes,.

la:verb:complector.html:
complector (conp-), plexus, 3, v. dep. (in signif. mostly coinciding with amplector), prop.,
to entwine around a person or thing (cf. amplector; class. in prose and poetry).
Lit.
Of persons, to clasp, embrace, as an expression of affection.
With acc.: vidi et illam et hospitem Conplexum atque ausculantem,: adcurrit; mediam mulierem complectitur,: tum ille artius puellam amplexus,: viri corpus,: (adulescentem) complexus osculatusque dimiserit,: suum maritum,: nepotes,: aliquem conplexa tenere, (17, 36); cf. .—Of parts of the person: dextram euntis,; ; cf. : infirmis membra lacertis,: genua. in supplication,: pedes alicujus,.—
With inter se: nosque inter nos esse conplexos,: conplecti inter se lacrimantes milites coepisse,; .—
With in vicem, .—
Absol.: nequeunt conplecti satis,: Phr. Conplectere. Di. Lubens, : contineri qum conplectar non queo,; ; —

(ε) With cum and abl., .—

In gen., to grasp, clasp, seize, encircle, surround, compass, enclose: (vitis) claviculis suis quasi manibus quicquid est nacta complectitur,: (orbis caelestis) extimus, qui reliquos omnis complectitur,: complexi terram maris,: ubi mollis amaracus illum (Ascanium) Floribus et dulci conplectitur umbrā,: vestis complectens undique corpus,: spatium,to mark out around for military purposes,; Auct. B. G. 8, 74; cf. of ploughing around,: aliquem obsidione, et saep.: caput digitis cruentis,: manibus eminentia saxa,: dexterā impendentes ramos,.—Of grasping an adversary in fight: quoad stans complecti posset atque contendere,: qui cum inter se complexi in terram ex equis decidissent... non prius distracti sunt, quam alterum anima relinqueret,in contention,.—
Trop.
Of sleep, to seize upon, enfold: sopor fessos complectitur artus,; cf.: me artior somnus conplexus est,.—
To embrace something intellectually as a whole, to comprehend, understand: aliquid cogitatione et mente,; cf. : deum et divinum animum cogitatione,: omne caelum totamque cum universo mari terram mente,; cf. ; : animo proxima quaeque meo,: rei magnitudinem animo,; ; ; cf. without acc.: cum conplector animo, quattuor reperio causas, etc.,.—Without mente, animo, etc.: perficies ut ego ista innumerabilia complectens nusquam labar?: totum genus judiciorum,: formam animi magis quam corporis,to consider,: aliquid memoriā,; ; and without memoria,.—
To comprehend a multitude of objects in discourse or in a written representation, to comprise, express, describe, represent, explain; with acc. and abl. or adv.: omnia alicujus facta oratione,: omnium rerum memoriam breviter libro,: orator autem sic illigat sententiam verbis, ut eam numero quodam complectatur et astricto et soluto,: omnia unā comprehensione,: plura semel,: pauca paucis,; cf. : sententiam his verbis,.—Esp. with sententiā, to sum up in a formal vote or decree (of speeches in the Senate): causas complectar ipsā sententiā, in the motion or decree itself, : sed ut aliquando sententiā complectar, ita censeo,.—Hence,
In philos. lang., to draw a conclusion, make an inference, ; ; cf. complexio.—
To embrace from love, to love, value, honor; to be addicted to, to care for; with acc. and abl.: aliquem honoribus et beneficiis suis,; cf.: eum beneficio,: aliquem summā benevolentiā,: hunc omni tuā comitate,: omnes caritate cives,: aliquem artā familiaritate,— Without abl.: hominem,. —Absol.: da te homini; complectetur,: quos fortuna complexa est,: philosophiam,; cf.: artes ingenuas,: causam eam,; cf. : otium,.—
To embrace, include: cari sunt parentes, cari liberi, propinqui, familiares, sed omnis omnium caritates patria una complexa est,: licet haec omnia complectatur eversio,; .—
(Causa pro effectu.) To take into possession, to seize, lay hold of, to make one's self master of (rare): (philosophiae) vis valet multum, cum est idoneam complexa naturam,: facultatem aliquam,; : plures provincias complexus sum quam alii urbes ceperunt,.!*? *
Act. collat form complecto, ĕre: quando convenit complectite, Pompon. ap. ; cf. P.—
complector, ti, in pass. signif.: invidiosā fortunā complecti, ap. P.: quo uno maleficio scelera omnia complexa esse videantur, (but in , and , the best read. is completur).

la:verb:complico.gloss: to fold or roll up or together
senses: to fold or roll up or together
la:verb:complico.html:
com-plĭco (conp-), āvi, ātum (postAug. ui, ĭtum; cf.: applico, explico, etc.), 1, v. a.,
to fold together, to fold up (rare but class.).
Prop.: rudentem,: armamenta,: epistulam,; : Diogenes se complicuit in dolio,: pedibus complicitis,; cf.: complicitus in genua,, p. 111, 3. —*
Trop.: si quis voluerit animi sui complicatam notionem evolvere (the figure borrowed from the folding together of books, letters, etc.),.

la:verb:comparo.gloss: to prepare something with zeal, care, make ready, set in order, furnish, provide
senses: to prepare something with zeal, care, make ready, set in order, furnish, provide
to procure, get, obtain, prepare, make, collect
la:verb:comparo.html:
compăro (conp-), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
compar
,
to couple together in the same relation, to connect in pairs, to pair, match, unite, join; constr. aliquid cum aliquā re, alicui rei, aliqua inter se, or absol.
Lit. (rare but class.).
In gen.: ut inter ignem et terram aquam deus animamque poneret, eaque inter se compararet et proportione conjungeret, ut, etc.,: comparari postremo,: ambo cum simul aspicimus, non possumus non vereri, ne male comparati sitis,: L. Volumnius cum Ap. Claudio consul est factus, priore item consulatu inter se conparati,: labella cum labellis,: quin meum senium cum dolore tuo conjungam et comparem, Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 90 Rib.).— Hence,
Esp. of combatants, for the usu. compono, to bring together to a contest, to match: ut ego cum patrono disertissimo comparer,: cum Aesernino Samnite Pacideianus comparatus,; Lucil. ap. : Scipio et Hannibal, velut ad supremum certamen comparati duces,: hunc Threci comparavit,.—
Trop.
To couple together in judgment.
To count one object fully equal to another, to place on the same footing, put on an equality with (rare but class.): neminem tibi profecto hominem ex omnibus aut anteposuissem umquam aut etiam comparassem, ap. ; cf. ; ; ; : cum quibus (hominibus) comparari sordidum,; so : et se mihi comparat Ajax?.—
In gen., to place together in comparison, to compare (the usu. signif. of the word in prose and poetry): homo quod rationis est particeps similitudines comparat,: majora, minora, paria,; : metaphora rei comparatur, quam volumus exprimere,.—With dat.: equi fortis et victoris senectuti, comparat suam,: si regiae stirpi comparetur ignobilis,: restat ut copiae copiis conparentur vel numero vel, etc.,: se majori pauperiorum turbae,: Periclem fulminibus et caelesti fragori comparat,; cf. : necesse est sibi nimium tribuat, qui se nemini comparat,: nec tantum inutilibus comparantur utilia, sed inter se quoque ipsa,; cf .—With cum and abl.: hominem cum homine et tempus cum tempore et rem cum re,; : cum illo... ceteris rebus nullo modo comparandus es,: cum meum factum cum tuo comparo,; ; : corporis commoda cum externis et ipsa inter se corporis,: longiorem orationem cum magnitudine utilitatis,: victoria, quae cum Marathonio possit comparari tropaeo,: totam causam nostram cum tota adversarii causā,; .—With ad: nec comparandus hic quidem ad illum est,: sed nihil comparandi causā loquar,I will institute no comparison,.— Hence,
With rel.-clause, to reflect, consider, judge; or to prove, show, by comparing (rare): id ego semper mecum sic agito et comparo, quo pacto magnam molem minuam, Att. ap. : cum comparetur, utrum, etc.,: comparando quam intestina corporis seditio similis esset irae plebis in patres, etc.,; cf. : deinde comparat, quanto plures deleti sint homines, etc.,.—
Comparare inter se, t. t., of colleagues in office, to agree together in respect to the division of duties, to come to an agreement (freq. in Liv., esp. of the consuls, who made an arrangement between themselves in respect to their provinces): inter se decemviri comparabant, quos ire ad bellum, quos praeesse exercitibus oporteret,: senatusconsultum factum est, ut consules inter se provincias Italiam et Macedoniam compararent sortirenturve,; ; ; 33, 43, 2; 26, 8, 8; 41, 6, 1: (consules) comparant inter se ut, etc.,; : ut consules sortirentur conparerentve inter se, uter, etc.,; of the tribunes of the people,; of the proprætors,.—
(In acc. with I. B.) Si scias quod donum huic dono contra comparet, opposes to this, .—Hence, * compărātē, adv., in or by comparison, comparatively: quaerere (opp. simpliciter),.

la:verb:compareo.gloss: to be evident or apparent; to be visible, appear
senses: to be evident or apparent; to be visible, appear
la:verb:compareo.html:
com-pārĕo (conp-), ui, 2, v. n.,
to be perfectly evident or apparent, to appear, be visible (class.).
Prop.: qui modo nusquam conparebas, nunc quom conpares peris,: ita ego ad omnis conparebo tibi res benefactis frequens ( = in omnibus rebus),: nec tamen ulla Comparebat avis, * : omnis suspitio in eos servos, qui non comparebant, commovebatur,: repente comparuit incolumis, et saep.: ornamenta orationis,; cf. : nequaquam argenti ratio conparet,agrees, is correct,; Orell. N. cr. —
Meton. (effectus pro causa), to be present, be in existence, to exist: et memor sum et diligens, ut quae imperes, conpareant,may be done,: signa et dona comparere omnia,: in Thucydide orbem modo orationis desidero, ornamenta comparent,: conquiri quae comparerent jussit,; so ; ; ; cf. ; ; .

la:verb:comprehendo.gloss: to lay hold of something on all sides; take or catch hold of, grasp, grip
senses: to lay hold of something on all sides; take or catch hold of, grasp, grip
to seize upon in a hostile manner, lay hold of; occupy, capture (of a place); arrest, detain, apprehend, catch; to intercept (a letter)
to discover, detect, come upon, reveal
to contain, comprise, to enclose, to include, to comprehend
to conjoin, to fuse with the thing that has come close
to be connected to a structure serving cognition as follows
la:verb:comprehendo.html:
com-prĕhendo (conp-; also com-prendo, very freq. in MSS. and edd.; cf. . In MSS. also comprae-hendo and compraendo, v. prehendo), di, sum, 3,
v. a., to lay hold of something on all sides; to take or catch hold of, seize, grasp, apprehend; to comprehend, comprise (class. in prose and poetry).
Prop.
In gen.: quid (opus est) manibus, si nihil comprehendendum est?: (vulva) non multo major quam ut manu comprehendatur,: cum (forfex) dentem comprehendere non possit,: mordicus manum eorum (elephantorum),: morsu guttura,: nuces modio,: naves,to join one to another, fasten together,; cf.: oras vulneris suturae comprehendunt,: comprehendunt utrumque et orant,: ter frustra comprensa manus effugit imago,; cf. aures,: nisi quae validissima (ovis), non comprehendatur (sc. stabulis) hieme,let none but the strongest be kept in the winter, Schneid.: naves in flumine Vulturno comprehensae,assembled together, put under an embargo,; so ; ; : ignem,to take, catch,; and in a reverse constr.: ignis robora comprendit,; cf.: opera flammā comprehensa,; and: avidis comprenditur ignibus agger,: loca vallo,; and absol.: comprehensa aedificia,.—
In partic.
To attack, seize upon in a hostile manner, to seize, lay hold of, arrest, catch, apprehend: aliquem pro moecho Comprehendere et constringere,; : tam capitalem hostem,: hominem,: nefarios duces,: Virginium,; cf. : praesidium Punicum,: hunc comprehenderant atque in vincula conjecerant,; : in fugā,.—Rarely of disease: comprehensus morbo,; cf.: comprehensi pestiferā lue,.—Of places, to occupy, seize upon: aliis comprehensis collibus munitiones perfecerunt,—*
Of things, to intercept'-epistulas, .—
To seize upon one, to apprehend him in any crime: fures,.—With inf.: qui interesse concentibus interdictis fuerint comprehensi, Cod. Th. 16, 4, 5.—Hence,
Transf. to the crime: nefandum adulterium,to discover, detect it,: res ejus indicio,.—
Of plants, to take root; of a graft: cum comprehendit (surculus),; so, in gen.,; ; .—
Of women, to conceive, become pregnant, = concipere: si mulier non comprehendit, etc.,—
Of a space, to contain, comprise, comprehend, include: ut nuces integras, quas uno modio comprehendere possis,: circuitus ejus triginta et duo stadia comprehendit,. —
In late medic. lang., of medicines, to combine: aliquid melle,; ; —
Of the range of a missile: quantum impulsa valet comprehendere lancea nodo,.—
Of the reach of a surgical instrument: si vitium in angusto est, quod comprehendere modiolus possit,—
Trop.
To comprehend by the sense of sight, to perceive, observe, see (very rare): aliquid visu,; and without visu: comprehendere vix litterarum apices,.—
To comprehend something intellectually, to receive into one's mind, to grasp, perceive, comprehend; with abl.: si quam opinionem jam mentibus vestris comprehendistis: si eam ratio convellet, si oratio labefactabit, etc., if any opinion has already taken root in your mind (the figure taken from the rooting of plants; v.supra, I. B. 3.), : omnes animo virtutes,; : animo haec tenemus comprehensa, non sensibus,: omnia animis et cogitatione,; cf. : aliquid mente,: aliquid memoriā,: qualis animus sit vacans corpore, intellegere et cogitatione comprehendere,: aliquid certis signis,: aliquid experimentis assiduis,.—Without abl.: esse aliquid, quod conprehendi et percipi posset,; : virtutum cognitio confirmat percipi et conprehendi multa posse,; 1, 11, 42.—
To comprehend or include in words; to comprise in discourse or in writing, to express, describe, recount, narrate, etc.: breviter paucis comprendere multa,; cf.: breviter comprehensa sententia,; : comprehendam brevi,: perinde ac si in hanc formulam omnia judicia conclusa et comprehensa sint,: (Cato) verbis luculentioribus et pluribus rem eandem comprehenderat,: ipsa natura circumscriptione quādam verborum comprehendit concluditque sententiam,: in eā (terrā) enim et lapis et harena et cetera ejus generis sunt in nominando comprehensa,: emplastra quoque, quae supra comprehensa sunt,; so absol.: ad veterum rerum nostrarum memoriam comprehendendam impulsi sumus,: aliquid dictis,: quae si comprendere coner,. —
Poet.: aliquid numero, to number, enumerate: neque enim numero comprendere refert,; ; cf.: numerum quorum comprendere non est,.—
To comprehend any one in affection, to bind to one's self, to put under obligation, to embrace with kindness (rare; mostly in Cic.): multos amicitiā, tueri obsequio, etc.,to have many friends,: adulescentem humanitate tuā,: quod omnibus officiis per se, per patrem, per majores suos totam Atinatem praefecturam comprehenderit,. 47.—
To shut in, include (late Lat.): spiritum in effigiem,: elementorum figurae humanā specie comprehensae,.

la:verb:compleo.gloss: to fill up, fill full, fill out; make up, complete
senses: to fill up, fill full, fill out; make up, complete
to occupy, set up a garrison (military)
la:verb:compleo.html:
com-plĕo (conp-), ēvi, ētum, 2 (contr. forms: complerunt, complerint, complerat, complesse, etc., for compleverunt, etc., very often), v. a.
pleo, whence suppleo, plenus
,
to fill up, fill full, fill out (class. in prose and poetry).
Lit., of material objects.
In gen., with acc. of place, vessel, etc., filled.
Alone: hostes fossam complent,; Auct. B. Hisp. 16; : tune aut inane quicquam putes esse, cum ita conpleta et conferta sint omnia, ut, etc.,: metu, ne compleantur navigia,: deducunt socii navis et litora conplent,: conplebant Laidos aedes (amatores),: corpora quae loca complerent,occupy space,: legiones cum loca Camporum complent,: milites complent murum,: vigiles domum Flavii complevere,; : scrobem ad medium,: non bene urnam,: vascula,: paginam,to fill out, write full,: speluncas, of the winds,.—
With abl. of material, etc.: fossas sarmentis et virgultis,: totum prope caelum... humano genere conpletum est,: mundum animorum multitudine,: bestiis omnium gentium circum conplere,: naufragorum trepidatione passim natantium flumen conpleverunt,: Hispanias Gallias Italiam monumentis ingentium rerum,: quos (gradus) ubi accusator concitatis hominibus complerat,: munus Apolline dignum libris,: late loca milite,: naves serpentibus,: amphoras plumbo,: statuas aëneas pecuniā,: horrea messibus,: complentur moenia et tecta maerentium turbā,: Palatium multitudine et clamoribus complebant,: virgultibus et cratibus et corporibus exanimis complere lossas,; cf. also: et terrae... stirpium renovatione complentur,.—
With gen.: conviviumque vicinorum cottidie conpleo,: cum completus jam mercatorum carcer esset,: quae causa... ararum conpleverit urbis,.—
Esp.
In milit. lang.
To make the army, a legion, etc., of a full number, to complete, fill up: legiones in itinere,: cohortes pro numero militum complet,; : legione completā per maniplos,.—
To man, fill with men: classem Romanam sociis navalibus,: naves colonis pastoribusque,; cf.: has (naves) sagittariis tormentisque compleverunt,: naves bis denas aut plures, Serv.—
To fill, impregnate: alias (mulieres),; .—
Transf., of light, sound, etc. (freq.).
To fill with light, maké full: ut cuncta suā luce conpleat (sol),: mundum suā luce,: terras largā luce,: orbem (luna),: lunae se cornua lumine complent,: quod maria ac terras omnis caelumque rigando Conpleat (sol),.—
To fill with sound, cause to resound, etc., to fill, make full: omnia clamoribus,: omnia vocibus,: nemus querellis,; cf.: nemus timendā voce,: aëra tinnitibus et murmure,: atria ululatu,: atria fremitu, et saep.: fremitu aequora, (3, 8), 37: aures (sonus),; cf. : caelum clamore,: aures sermonibus, Claud. Cons. Prob. et Olyb. 31: clamor omnia variis terrentium ac paventium vocibus complet, .—
Of odors, etc.: omnia primo motu ac spiritu suo, vini, unguenti, corporis odore complesset,; cf. . —
Transf., to cover, overwhelm: Dianam (i. e. simulacrum) coronis et floribus,i. e. to deck, adorn,: vortentibus Telebois telis conplebantur corpora,.—
To fill, sate with food or drink: multo cibo et potione,: se flore Liberi,: haec avis scribitur conchis se solere conplere,.—
Trop.
To supply fully, furnish abundantly: exercitum omni copiā,—
To fill with any notion, story, desire, humor, passion: completi sunt animi auresque vestrae, me... obsistere, etc.,: reliquos (milites) bonā spe,: aliquem gaudio,: taedio,: animos robore,: omnia luctu,: omnia terrore,: cuncta pavore,—With gen.: aliquem erroris et dementiae,: aliquem flagitii et formidinis,.—
To make complete or perfect, to finish; of a promise, to fulfil it: lustrationem (annuam) menstruo spatio (luna),; cf. : his rebus completis legiones reduci jussit, (Dinter, ex conj., comparatis): nocturnum erat sacrum, ita ut ante mediam noctem conpleretur,: studia,: conplent ea beatissimam vitam,; cf. ; : summam promissi,: rerum humanarum sorte completā,—
Of time, to finish, complete: Gorgias centum et septem conplevit annos,: cum VII. et LXX. annos complesset,: Corvinus centesimum annum complevit,; Lact. Op. Dei, 4, 3; cf.: sua fata,: sua tempora,: quinque saecula vitae suae,: materna tempora,i. e. the time of pregnancy,; cf. : semel quadrigis, semel desultore misso, vix unius horae tempus utrumque curriculum conplebat,.—Hence, complētus, a, um, P. a. *
Prop., filled full, full: alveus Tiberis ruderibus, * .—
Trop., complete, perfect: completus et perfectus verborum ambitus,.—* Comp., .

la:verb:comperio.gloss: to learn, discover, ascertain or find out
senses: to learn, discover, ascertain or find out
la:verb:comperio.html:
com-pĕrĭo, pĕri, pertum, 4, v. a.
root par-, of paro, pario; cf. 2. comparo, and aperio, operio, etc.; by others separated from these words and referred to root per-, of πειράω, peritus, periculum; but cf. Corss. Ausspr. II. 410
, lit.,
to disclose wholly, lay open (a fact), without the access. idea of communicating the thing disclosed (which aperio expresses; v. aperio); to obtain a knowledge of a thing, to find out with certainty, to have or gain certain information, to ascertain, learn, etc. (class. in prose and poetry): certo comperi,: cum indicia mortis se comperisse manifesto et manu tenere diceret,: hoc,: stellarum ortus,: de amore hoc comperit,: nihil de hoc (Sullā) consul comperi,; : postquam de scelere filii comperit,; —With inf. and acc., : posteaquam comperit eum posse vivere,: hanc gentem Clusium inde venisse comperio,; : diram qui contudit hydram, comperit invidiam supremo fine domari, * : ubi comperi ex eis qui, etc.,: aliquid ex multis,: ex litteris,: per exploratores,; ; : certis auctoribus,: nihil testibus, nihil tabulis, nihil aliquo gravi argumento,; : a quo ut rem gestam comperit,: quae ex fratre compererat nuntiari regi jubet,: ut postea ex captivis comperit,; ; .—Cicero, on account of the frequent repetition of the phrase omnia comperi, in the trial of Catiline, was often bantered by his contemporaries; hence: (Clodius) me tantum comperisse omnia criminabatur,; cf. .—With depend. question: dolo an vere cunctatus, parum comperimus,; .—
Esp. freq. in part. perf. pass.: Oppianici facinus manifesto compertum atque deprehensum,: non ego haec incertis jacta rumoribus adfero ad vos, sed comperta et explorata,; cf. ; : sintne haec investigata, comperta, patefacta per me,: pecuniam ex aerario scribae viatoresque aedilicii clam egessisse per indicem comperti,discovered,: compertus adulterare matronas, : uxorem in stupro generi compertam,detected,.—Also with the gen. of the crime: compertus stupri,; : probri,: sacrilegii,: flagitii,; : de his haud facile compertum narraverim,give certain information,: qui ex fratre comperta ipsi nuntiasset,: haec ex vate comperta nuntiabat,.— In abl. absol.: comperto lege Gabiniā Bithyniam et Pontum consuli datam, Fragm. ap. P.; so and 7; 33, 5, 4; ; ; fin.; 14, 57.—So, also, compertum habeo and compertum mihi est, I know full well: quod de his duobus habuerint compertum,; so ; fin.: pro comperto polliceri,as certain,.—Hence, compertē, adv., on good authority; only ; and in comp., .

la:verb:compono.gloss: to arrange, compile, compose, make up, organize, order
senses: to arrange, compile, compose, make up, organize, order
to pacify, allay, settle, calm, appease, quiet, tranquillize, reconcile
la:verb:compono.html:
com-pōno (conp-), pŏsŭi (COMPOSEIVERVNT, C. I. L. 1, 199, 2), pŏsĭtum (compostus, Lorenz; ; Lucil. ap. ; Varr ap. ), 3, v. a.,
to put, place, lay, bring or set together, to unite, join, connect, collect, aggregate, compose, to order, arrange, adjust, etc. (class. and very freq.).
In gen., of different objects.
To bring into union, gather, collect, put together.
Of things in gen.: aridum lignum,: compositā fronde,: uvas in tecto in cratibus,: in quo (loco) erant ea conposita, quibus rex te numerare constituerat,: (amomum) manipulatim leniter componitur,: amphoras in culleum,: ligna in caminum,.—
To bring into contact, fit together, join: quid... in operibus manu factis tam compositum tamque compactum et coagmentatum inveniri potest?: cum poclo bibo eodem, amplector, labra labellis conpono, Lucil. ap. : tum latus conponit lateri et cum pectore pectus, p. 260, 30: conponens manibusque manus atque ori bus ora,: Mercurio Sais fertur Virgineum conposuisse latus,; cf. caput,.—Hence, of broken limbs, etc., med. t. t., to set: ossa,: jugulum, et saep.—
Esp., to pack up for a journey, etc.: omnia composta sunt quae donavi,: i ergo intro et compone quae tecum simul Ferantur,: dum tota domus raedā componitur unā,.—
Of persons: is (Saturnus) genus indocile ac dispersum montibus altis Composuit,: et tabula una duos poterit componere amantes, (3, 22, 13); cf. II. C. 5. infra.—
To set in opposition.
To bring together in hostility, to oppose, to couple, pair, match in combat (cf. compositio, III.); esp. of gladiators, etc.: Samnis, spurcus homo, cum Pacideiano conponitur, optimus multo Post homines natos gladiator qui fuit unus, Lucil. Sat. ap. ; cf. : Rupili et Persi par pugnat, uti non Compositum melius cum Bitho Bacchius, Orell. ad loc.: staturam habere Threcis cum Threce conpositi,, praef. 8; and in gen.: si quis casus duos inter se bonos viros composuerit,: cuive virūm mallem memet componere,: componimur Vecordi Decio,: hunc fatis,: cum ventis, pelagique furentibus undis Composuit mortale genus,; and fig.: pergis pugnantia secum Frontibus adversis componere,: ecce par deo dignum, vir fortis cum fortunā malā conpositus,: non illa (rhetorice) secum ipsa componitur,; and of a judicial contest: accita Epicharis et cum indice composita,confronted,; .—
To oppose by way of comparison, to compare, contrast.
With acc. and dat.: quid est, cur componere ausis mihi te aut me tibi? Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 147 Rib.): nec divis homines componier aequom'st,: composita dicta evolvunt, Quae cum componas, dicta factis discrepant, Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 48 Rib.): si parva licet conponere magnis,: parvis conponere magna solebam,; ,

416: audes cladi componere nostrae, Nympha, tuam?: divinis humana,.—

With acc. and cum: ubi Metelli dicta cum factis conposuit,: causam suam cum causā adversarii. .
In partic.
Of the parts of a whole, or of a whole as made up of parts.
To bring together, compose, compound, make up, mix, construct.
With ex: exercitus ejus conpositus ex variis gentibus,: genus humanum ex corpore et animā conpositum,: liber ex alienis orationibus compositus,: antidoton... ex multis atque interim contrariis quoque inter se effectibus,: ex quo (umore) componi debet (medicamentum),—
With abl.: mensam gramine,.—
With acc. alone: medicamentum,; .—
Esp., of buildings, etc., to construct, build: qui cuncta conposuit,i. e. the Creator,: urbem,: illa (templa) deis, Burm. ad loc.: aggere conposito tumuli,: deletas Thebas,.—
Of words, to compound: vitilitigatores ex vitiis et litigatoribus, Plin. praef. § 32: verba composita (opp. simplicia),.—
Of writings, speeches, etc.
To compose, write, construct (very freq.): leges,: compone hoc, quod postulo, de argento: de reliquo videro,: quartum librum,: libros,; : libellos,: actiones,; : argumentum,: edictum eis verbis,: edictum eorum arbitratu,, § 119: artes,books of instruction,; : artificium,: commentarium consulatūs mei,; : quarum (litterarum) exemplum,: quandam disciplinae formulam,: stipulationum et judiciorum formulas,: interdictum,: poëma,; cf. ; : senatūs consultum,: testimonium,: verba ad religionem deorum immortalium,: de judicialibus causis aliqua,: aliquid de ratione dicendi, id. prooem. 1: quae de ortu vitāque Scapulae composita erant,: Apion... inmortalitate donari a se scripsit ad quos aliqua conponebat, Plin. praef. § 25: carmen,: carmina,; : epistulas,: litteras nomine Marcelli,; : orationem habere ad conciliandos plebis animos conpositam,: blanditias tremulā voce,: meditata manu verba trementi,: versus,: mollem versum,: cantus,: in morem annalium,: orationes adversus aliquem,: litteras ad aliquem,; : probra in Gaium,; 14, 50: multa et atrocia in Macronem, (38) et saep.—
Transf., of the subjects, etc., treated, to write about, treat, celebrate: tuas laudes,: res gestas,: tempora Iliaca,: bellum Troicum,: Juli Africani vitam componendo, spem hominibus fecisti plurium ejus modi librorum,: veteres populi Romani res,: Neronis res,; 11, 11.—
From the notion of closing.
To put away, put aside, put in place: armamentis conplicandis, conponendis studuimus,i. e. folding up the sails and lowering the masts,: (tempus) ad componenda armamenta expediendumque remigem,: vela contrahit malosque inclinat et simul armamenta componens, etc.,: arma,: tristes istos conpone libellos,put aside,.—
To store up, put away, collect: nec... Aut conponere opes norant aut parcere parto,: ego conposito securus acervo Despiciam dites,; so fig.: condo et compono quae mox depromere possim,.— So esp. to preserve, pack, put up fruits, meat, etc., for future use: pernas,: tergora (suis),: siccatos coliculos, : caepam in fidelia,: herbas,: poma,: olivas,: herbam ollā novā,: faenum,: fructus in urceis, capsellis,, §1.—
Of the ashes or remains of the dead, to adjust, lay out, to collect and inurn, inter, bury: tu mea conpones et dices, ossa, Properti, Haec tua sunt, (3, 19, 19): cinerem,: cinerem ossaque,: sic ego conponi versus in ossa velim,.—Hence, in gen., of persons, to bury: quem... prope cognatos conpositum cineres,: omnes composui (meos),: compositi busta avi,: Pisonem Verania uxor... T. Vinium Crispina filia composuere,: componi tumulo eodem,: toro Mortua componar,: alto Conpositus lecto,: aliquem terrā,.—
To lay at rest, compose, quiet.
Of things: omnia noctis erant placidā composta quiete, Varr. Atac. ap. : cum mare compositum est,: aquas,: fessum tumentes Composuit pelagus ventis patientibus undas,.—
Of persons: nec vigilantibus, sed etiam quiete compositis,: ubi jam thalamis se conposuere,: defessa membra,: si bene conpositus somno vinoque jacebit,.—
To end strife, confusion, etc., to compose, pacify, allay, settle, calm, appease, quiet, tranquillize, reconcile, etc., that which is disturbed or at variance.
With personal object: aversos amicos,: ceteros clementiā,: comitia praetorum,; : juvenes concitatos,; cf.: barbarūm animos,: gentem,.—Esp. of the mind: prima (pars philosophiae) conponit animum,: argumentum conpositae mentis,; ; : mentem somno,: religio saevas componit mentis,.—
Of places, countries, etc.: C. Caesar componendae Armeniae deligitur,: Campaniam,: Daciam,.—
With abstr. or indef. objects: si possum hoc inter vos conponere,; cf.: vides, inter nos sic haec potius cum bonā Ut componamus gratiā quam cum malā?: gaudens conponi foedere bellum,; so, bellum,; ; ; ; Asin. ap. : bella,: cum vellet pro communi amico controversias regum componere,: uti per colloquia omnes controversiae componantur,fin.: curas,; : lites,: seditionem civilem,: statum Orientis,: Romanus Ardeae turbatas seditione res... composuit,; : legatorum res et bello turbatas,: res Germanicas,: discordias,: compositis praesentibus,: odia et certamina,.—Less freq. transf., with the result as object: pacem componi volo Meo patri cum matre,: si pax cum Carthaginiensibus componi nequisset,: at me conpositā pace fefellit Amor,: pax circa Brundusium composita,: pacem cum Pyrrho,; cf. D. 2. infra.—
Absol.: coheredes mei conponere et transigere cupiebant,; and so impers. pass.: posteaquam id quod maxime volui fieri non potuit, ut componeretur,: Pompei summam esse... voluntatem, ut componeretur atque ab armis discederetur,.—
Hence, to set right, to set in or restore to the proper place or condition, to adjust, etc.
In gen., to arrange, adjust, order, set in order: aulaeis se superbis Aureā spondā, of one's attitude on a couch,: ad ictum militaris gladii conpositā cervice,: diductis aedificia angulis vidimus moveri iterumque conponi,: si ad rem pertinet, quomodo caelo adfecto conpositisque sideribus quodque animal oriatur,: tibi enim gratias agebat, quod signa componenda suscepisses,.—
Esp., milit. t. t.: se ad confligendum, Sisenn. ap. Non p. 257, 13: exercitum in hibernaculis, Sali J. 103, 1: in secundā (acie) cohortis, id. H. inc. Fragm. 44 Dietsch: stabant conpositi suis quisque ordinibus (opp. incompositi),: conpositi numero in turmas,: cunctos licentiā vagos compositus invadit = compositis ordinibus,: agmen,; 5, 1; : ordines,: vagos paventesque Vitellianos, sua quemque apud signa, componunt,: pugnae exercitum,: auxilia in numerum legionis, Nipp. ad loc.: equitem per turmas,: insidias in montibus,.—
Of the order of words in language: quam lepide λέξεις compostae! ut tesserulae omnes Arte pavimento atque emblemate vermiculato, Lucil. ap. ; id. ap. ; cf. sq.: ut aptior sit oratio, ipsa verba compone,.—
With reference to orderly appearance, etc., of the clothing, hair; the expression of the countenance, etc., to lay, smooth, adjust: suon quisque loco'st? Vide capillum, satin compositu'st commode?: composito et delibuto capillo,: comas,: crines,: ne turbarentur comae, quas componi, etc.,: togam,to lay in proper folds,; ; cf.: nec tamen ante adiit... Quam se composuit, quam circumspexit amictus,: pulvinum facili manu,; cf. torum,: jam libet componere voltus,: vultu composito, ne laeti excessu principis, etc.,; ; cf.: (Tiberius) compositus ore,: vultum naturā horridum... efferabat, componens ad speculum in omnem terrorem,distorting,.—
In gen., to adjust, arrange, regulate, for the expression of something, or to accord with something; usu. ad aliquid: ad abstinentiam rursus, non secus ac modo ad balineum animum vultumque conposui,: orationis ipsius vultus ad id, quod efficere intendimus, compositus,: utrāque manu ad modum aliquid portantium compositā,: ge. stum oratoris ad similitudinem saltationis,: figuram ad imitationem alterius scripturae,: nec ad votum composita civitas,: cuncta ad decorem inperi conposita,: cunctis ad tristitiam conpositis,. —Less freq. with dat.: voltus conponere famae Taedet,to adapt,: venturis carbasa ventis,: me quoque mittendis rectum componite telis,. —With in: Nero itinera urbis... veste servili in dissimulationem sui compositus pererrabat,disguised, made up,. —
To bring to a particular form or condition, to dispose, arrange, set in order, contrive, devise, prepare.
With acc.: ego itinera sic composueram, ut Nonis Quinctilibus Puteolis essem,: quod adest memento Componere aequus,: conpositā atque constitutā re publicā,: necdum compositis maturisve satis consiliis,: (diem) totum in considerandā causā componendāque posuisse,: tempus in cognoscendis componendisque causis consumere,: ex sententiā omnibus rebus paratis conpositisque,; : in senatu cuncta longis aliorum principatibus composita statim decernuntur,: dum quae forent firmando Neronis imperio componuntur,.—
With ad or in and acc. of the purpose for which, or the example according to which, etc.: cum alteri placeat auspicia ista ad utilitatem esse rei publicae conposita,: omnia ad voluptatem multitudinis inperitae,: animum ad omnes casus,; : satis igitur in hoc nos componet multa scribendi exercitatio,: cultum victumque non ad nova exempla conponere, sed ut majorum mores suadent,. —
To arrange in agreement with others, to agree upon, contrive, devise, invent, conspire to make, etc.
In gen.: eum allegaverunt, suom qui servom diceret Cum auro esse apud me: conposita est fallacia,

Ut, etc., : quin jam virginem Despondi: res composita'st,: ita causa componitur, ut item palaestritae Bidini peterent ab Epicrate hereditatem,: societatem praedarum cum latronibus conposuisse, Dietsch: crimen ab inimicis Romae conpositum,: conpositis inter se rebus,: ita conposito dolo digrediuntur,: conposito jam consilio,: ceteri proditores ea quae composita erant exspectabant; convenerat autem, etc.,: sub noctem susurri Compositā repetantur horā,: ictum jam foedus, et omnes Conpositae leges,: compositis notis,: crimen ac dolum ultro,: proditionem,: seditionem,: insidias,; ; : pacem componere, v. B. 5. supra.—

With rel.-clause: cum summā concordiā, quos dimitterent, quos retinerent, composuerunt,.—
With inf.: ii, secretis conloquiis conponunt Gallos concire,.—
Pass. impers.: ut domi compositum cum Marcio erat,.—(ε) With ut and subj.: compositum inter ipsos ut Latiaris strueret dolum,; cf. P. a. subst.—
In gen., to feign, invent, devise, contrive, in order to deceive or delude, etc.: composita dicta, Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 47 Rib.): ne tu istic hodie malo tuo conpositis mendaciis Advenisti,: nec bene mendaci risus conponitur ore, (3, 7, 3): sed vobis facile'st verba et conponere fraudes,: insidias in me conponis inanes, (3, 30), 19: compositas insidias fatoque evitatas ementitur,: si haec fabulosa et composita videntur,; : quae ut augendae famae composita, sic reliqua non in obscuro habentur,; cf.: vetustatem, ut cetera, in majus conponentem altores Jovis celebravisse,exaggerating, Dietsch.—Part. perf. with in and acc., pretending, assuming the appearance or expression: (Domitianus) paratus simulatione, in adrogantiam compositus audiit preces,: is in maestitiam compositus,; : in securitatem,.—Rarely with ad: tunc compositus ad maestitiam,.— Hence, P. a.: compŏsĭtus (-postus), a, um.
Well-arranged, ordered, or constituted, orderly, regular: quae (injuria) dum foris sunt, nil videtur mundius, Nec magis compositum quicquam nec magis elegans,: admiratus sum ... σύγχυσιν litterularum, quae solent tuae compositissimae et clarissimae esse, : acrior impetu atque animis quam compositior ullo ordine pugna fuit,: intellegitur, etiamsi non adjecero, conpositum ordinatumque fore talem virum,: composita et quieta et beata respublica,. —Of writings: quare in his quoque libris erant eadem aliqua... omnia vero compositiora et elaborata,; cf.: illa quae curam fatentur et ficta atque composita videri etiam volunt,elaborate,—Transf., of the orator himself: si aut compositi oratoris bene structam collocationem dissolvas permutatione verborum,.—
Fitly disposed for any purpose, prepared, apt, fit, adapted, qualified, suitable, ready: perficiam ut nemo umquam paratior, vigilantior, compositior ad judicium venisse videatur,; so, equus bene naturā compositus,.— With ad or in and acc., or with dat.: arte quādam ab juventā in ostentationem (virtutum) compositus, Weissenb. ad loc.: alius historiae magis idoneus, alius compositus ad carmen,: aeque in adulationem compositus (sacerdos),: (Attici) non maxime ad risum compositi,: naturā atque arte compositus alliciendis etiam Muciani moribus,.—
Quiet, peaceful, undisturbed, calm, composed, unimpassioned, etc.: ut peractis quae agenda fuerint salvo jam et composito die possis ibi manere,: lenis et nitidi et compositi generis amatores,: actio,: aetas,mature, sedate,: adfectus mites atque compositi, : supercilium (opp. erectum),: repetitio eorum (civium) labefactabat compositam civitatem,.—
Compound, composite, made up of parts (opp. simplex): verba,; ; : voces,; cf. ; .—Hence, subst.: compŏsĭ-tum (conp-), i, n., that which is agreed, an agreement, compact, etc.; only abl. in the phrases,
Ex composito, according to agreement, by agreement, in concert, Dietsch: tum ex composito orta vis,; ; ; 40, 48, 4; ; .—
De composito, by agreement, ; and,
More rarely in the same sense, composito alone, ; ; .—Hence also adv.: compŏsĭtē (conp-), in an orderly, regular, or skilful manner, orderly, regularly, properly (class. but rare; not in Quint.): ambulare,: indutus,: composite et apte dicere,: composite, ornate, copiose eloqui,: composite atque magnifice casum reipublicae miserati,: bene et composite disseruit,.—Comp.: compositius cuncta quam festinantius agerent,.

la:noun:compositum.gloss: that which is agreed; an agreement, compact, etc.
senses: that which is agreed; an agreement, compact, etc.

la:pron:complures.html:
com-plūres (conp-), a, and (mostly ante-class.) ia;
gen. ium (cf. ; Charis. pp. 56 and 100 P.; Don.), adj., more than one, not a few, several, very many; as adj. or subst., wholly without comp. force (freq. and class.).
Adj.
Nom.: complures consules,: Volcani,; al.: mulieres complures,: fana compluria, Cato ap. Don. l. l.: nova, l. l.: genera, ap. Don. l. l.: scyphorum paria complura,; so, genera ambiguorum, (al. plura): loca,: sacella publica,.—
Gen.: vita excellentium virorum complurium,—
Dat.: ut compluribus tonsoribus operam daret,.—
Acc.: servos complures,; so, menses,: dies,; : alios, * .—(ε) Abl.: ratibus compluribus factis, Oud. N. cr.; 8, 14 ib. et saep.— (ζ) Sup.: buceta complurima, Hertz.—
As subst.
complūres, ĭum, m. and f., several, many persons, etc.: Graecis institutionibus eruditi,; : (ea) compluribus narravit,: mandata ad complures dare,: complures hostium,.—
complūra, ium, n., many things: complura ne posui quidem, Caecil. ap. : ejusdem generis complura,

la:verb:comprobo.gloss: to approve wholly of something; to assent to, sanction, or acknowledge
senses: to approve wholly of something; to assent to, sanction, or acknowledge
to prove, establish, attest, make good, show, confirm, or verify something to others as true, good, excellent, virtuous, etc.
la:verb:comprobo.html:
com-prŏbo (conp-), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
Subject., to approve wholly of something, to assent to, sanction, acknowledge (class and very freq., esp in prose): istam tuam sentent. am laudo vehementissimeque comprobo,: decretum consulum,, D, 14 sq.: orationem omnium assensu,; cf. ; : consensu potius eruditorum quam puerorum amore comprobari, et saep.: has comproba tabulas,: ne domesticis quidem exemplis docti numen deorum comprobabimus?; .—
Object., to prove, establish, attest, make good, show, confirm, verify something to others as true, good, excellent, virtuous, etc.: ut beneficium verbis initum nunc re comprobes,; cf. : nec hoc oratione solum, sed multo magis vita et factis et moribus conprobavit,: patris dictum sapiens temeritas filii comprobavit,: comprobat hominis consilium fortuna,; cf. * : rem alicujus testimonio,; cf.: indicio conprobato,: perceleri (servi) interitu esse ab hoc comprobatum venenum,the quality of the poison was tested,.

senses: to compel, reduce to a certain condition or state by force
la:verb:compello#2.html:
